newsitem.title: FRANCE: Seguin says France's political system in crisis.
newsitem.headline: Seguin says France's political system in crisis.

text.p: Outgoing Gaullist National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin said Sunday's parliamentary election, which the Left won, showed France's entire political system was in crisis.

"The circumstances and events of this early election cannot hide the essential fact: our whole political system is in crisis. This reality applies to all, winners and losers. Indeed it is hard to know who to pity more," said Seguin, who would have been prime minister if the centre-right had retained power.

"As for me...I am determined to put all my strength at the service of my country in a parliamentary opposition that I expect to be loyal and true to the principles upon which the president of the Republic was elected," Seguin said.

"With all those who share the same concept of France, of France in Europe, in order to prepare for a different tomorrow, I am determined, utterly determined to create the right political conditions," he added.

President Jacques Chirac had anointed the Eurosceptic Gaullist Seguin and free-marketeer ex-finance minister Alain Madelin to lead the conservatives' election campaign after Prime Minister Alain Juppe took the blame for the first round defeat and agreed to resign.
Seguin had criticised Juppe's austerity policies to fulfil the criteria for the single European currency, calling for a more expansionary economic policy giving top priority to jobs.
